findings.description: The bucket sets no ACL restricting access and has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, and the inline comment states the bucket is public. Objects, including the uploaded customer master data, are exposed to anonymous readers.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects containing customer data are stored without enforced server-side encryption.
No logging block is configured, so unauthorised access to this publicly exposed bucket leaves no audit trail for detection or forensics.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so objects in a publicly exposed bucket can be overwritten or deleted with no recovery path or tamper evidence.
No bucket policy enforcing aws:SecureTransport is attached, so objects in this public bucket may be retrieved over plaintext HTTP.

A file named customer-master.xlsx, likely containing customer PII, is uploaded into aws_s3_bucket.data, which is publicly accessible and unencrypted; no per-object encryption (kms_key_id/server_side_encryption) is specified either.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for a bucket holding financial data, leaving stored objects without enforced encryption at rest.
No logging block is configured, so access to sensitive financial data is not auditable.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so financial objects can be overwritten or deleted without recovery, undermining integrity and anti-tamper controls.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so a later bucket policy or ACL change could silently expose financial data publicly.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects are stored without enforced server-side encryption.
No logging block is configured, leaving no audit trail of object access for this bucket.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so future ACL or policy changes could expose the bucket without a defence-in-depth guardrail.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so data science datasets are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, leaving no guardrail against accidental public exposure of datasets.
The log bucket relies solely on the 'log-delivery-write' ACL with no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so a future ACL or policy change could expose aggregated audit logs publicly.
